Commentary.Commentary: We didn't expect that it will be such an easy walk in the park for Pakistan but Zimbabwe are so much morally deflated due to their poor form that this was on the cards. The series is already gone for the home side but there is something called as pride. To uphold that, they will need to play out of their skins against a team which is in its elements. Join us for the 4th ODI on 20th July in Bulawayo at 0915 Local (0715 GMT) to catch all the action. Till then, cheers!

Pakistan skipper, Sarfraz Ahmed says that he is very pleased about the performance. Appreciates Junaid Khan and Faheem Ashraf for the way they bowled. States that Ashraf was on the money and his batting is a plus for the side as well. Mentions that he will try different combinations and give other players a chance in the remaining two games.
The Man of the Match has been awarded to Faheem Ashraf for his maiden 5-fer in ODIs. He was belligerent with the ball, breaking the backbone of the hosts.

Zimbabwe skipper, Hamilton Masakadza says that it was a forgettable game for them. Mentions that they would try to rectify their mistakes and improve themselves. States that more application is needed by the batsmen. Ends by saying that he hopes that his boys will fire in the next game and give their bowlers something to play for.

However, Fakhar Zaman was his free-flowing self once he got his eye in and played some pleasing strokes to take the tourists home along with Babar Azam with utmost ease. Kudos to the Pakistan bowlers for setting it up with a belligerent performance. Nothing much to write about the hosts. They didn't build any partnerships and were found wanting.

It has been a crushing victory for Pakistan, their biggest ever win in terms of balls remaining. With that, they have sealed the 5-match ODI series here itself. After bowling out Zimbabwe for their lowest total in Bulawayo, 67 to be precise, it was always going to be a formality for the visitors to chase it down. Blessing Muzarabani and Richard Ngarava were on the money initially with the former sending Imam-ul-Haq back on the first ball.

FOUR! And that's the game! Fakhar Zaman finishes things off with a superb boundary. Flicks the ball firmly through the mid-wicket region to send it across the fence for a boundary. A crushing victory, PAKISTAN WIN BY 9 WICKETS, WITH 241 BALLS TO SPARE!

Misfield and FOUR! Should have been two, but Blessing gifts a couple more. Short ball, Zaman pulls it through mid-wicket. Muzarabani out in the deep moves to his right, gets low to stop it but lets it through him for a boundary.
FOUR! Back of a length on off, Fakhar Zaman swings across the line and pulls it from the inner half through backward square leg. Boundary.
Slaps the cut behind point, towards third man and jogs to the other end to complete a single.
Thrown out wide outside off, Azam attempts to reach out for it but misses.
Fuller in length on off, a positive punch to covers, but it's straight to the fielder. Just 12 needed for Pakistan to win this game and the series.
Wide! Blessing hurls it fine down the leg side, the umpire signals wide.

FOUR! Zaman wants to waste no time in putting this game to bed. Finds the boundary line for the fourth time in this over. Back of a length outside off, he stands tall this time and cracks it through point on this occasion.
FOUR! Third of the over. A little too full on off, angling away, Zaman is loving this. He plants his front foot forward and drills it straight back down the ground.
Fullish length delivery outside off, played to covers for nothing.
FOUR! Consecutive boundaries for Zaman! Has room offered to him outside off, he stands tall and goes up and over point. Third man tried cutting it off but failed in his attempt to do so.

FOUR! A little bit of width and that's all Zaman needs to put it away. On a length, outside off, the left-hander smashes it through the gap in the covers, leaving the fielders with no chance to stop it.
Short and wide, it's smacked right off the middle, but straight to the cover fielder.
Wide! Back of a length down the leg side, wide signalled. Which is a bit strange given there was some noise as the ball went past Babar on his attempted flick shot. Not sure what happened there.
Offers a firm punch from the back foot to the man positioned at mid off.
Back of a length on middle, tamely pulled along the ground in front of square leg.
Full in length outside off, Babar defends it off the outer half to point.
Back of a length shaping away, outside off, punched softly in front of cover.
Marginally ahead of a length, on middle and off, works it off the inner half in front of square leg. Quick single results.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! All about the timing on that! Nicely done. Angling in on a length on the pads, Azam flicks it elegantly past the diving square leg fielder for a boundary.
Uses the angle and dabs it with an open face towards point for a run.
Darts it on the hips, with a little swivel Zaman pulls it to fine leg. The fielder there is a bit sloppy to get down, so the batsmen take two.
Top edge but it's safe! Back of a length on middle, Zaman looks to pull but edges it high over the keeper's head. Falls safely in the fine leg region and comes back for the second.
Full and swinging away outside off, Fakhar drives it to mid off.
Short of a good length on off, a front foot slap-pull from Babar Azam right back at the bowler. Just 40 away from a win now, Pakistan.
A bit wider outside off, pushed away for nothing.
Positions himself perfectly behind the line and guards it out.
FOUR! Third of the innings. Seems this Pakistan pair has found its rhythm. Back of a length outside off, Babar cracks it square through point. Beats the fielder and finds the fence with ease.
Outside off on a length, dabbed to point with an open face for a quick one.
FOUR! Short but it's not short enough. Sits up nicely for an in-form Fakhar Zaman as he swivels and pulls it powerfully through square leg along the turf. Superb shot. Second boundary of the innings.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Stays back in his crease and blocks.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. One run added to the total.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
ANOTHER WIDE. This time it is down the leg side, a flick shot missed.
FOUR! Full and outside off, Azam drives this straight back down the ground for a boundary!
WIDE. The batsman watches the bouncer go way above his head. The umpire signals a wide.
WIDE. An attempted bouncer which was well over head height. Wide signalled by the umpire.
The skipper is being treated now. We can see a bruise on his left palm.

EDGED, BUT DROPPED! Nearly a second wicket for Zimbabwe. It is on a length, slightly wide outside off, Zaman looks to drive but gets a thick outside edge. The ball flies towards wide second slip where Hamilton Masakadza looks to dive, stretches out his left hand, but the ball bursts through. A single to third man.
Back of a length on off, met with a straight blade in defense.
Fired in full, outside the line of off stump, driven to the cover fielder.
Pushes this gently just wide of mid off and calls his partner through for a quick single.
On the fourth stump line, Zaman is half-forward to block it out.
Shouts for a leg before, but it's turned down. Always going down leg. Ngarava angles it on leg, it keeps going down and catches Zaman on the pads as he misses his flick.
Serves it on a good length on the off stick, Zaman punches it away towards covers from within the crease.
Fuller in length in line of the stumps, driven off the inner half to mid on.
Angling back in on middle and leg, Babar flicks it off his pads towards backward square leg. Chisoro there does well to dive to his right and stop the ball from going past him.
Stays right behind the line and keeps it out.
Just ahead of a length, close to off, defended out safely.
Coming back into Zaman, he nudges it towards mid-wicket for a single.

It may not reach the fence, but it'll be enough to fetch him three. Full outside off, Babar drives it crisply through the covers. The outfield is a bit slow, so the fielder chasing it is allowed to pull it back inside the rope.
Wide! Shortish ball down the leg side, the right-hander tries to help the pull fine down the leg side but misses. Wide called.

Clocked on the helmet yet again. What's happening today? Fakhar Zaman the man on the receiving end this time. He looks fine, but since no chances are taken with head injuries these days, the physio comes out to have a look at him.

OUCH! Saw it happen in the first innings, it's happened again now. Zaman takes a blow on the helmet from the newcomer Ngarava. Short on off, the southpaw looks to take the pull on but the ball rises too quickly on him to hit him on the side.
Shortish on middle and leg, pushed away off the back foot just wide of mid on for a single.
Good length delivery angling away, outside off, Babar drives but gets an inside edge behind to the keeper on the bounce.
Cracked but straight to the fielder. Full ball outside off, Babar Azam middles this but straight to cover-point.
On a good length, attacking the stumps this time, another defensive shot presented in response.
Moving away from a good length around off, Babar once again hangs his bat close to his body and blocks it out.
Richard Ngarava to bowl from the other end with the second new ball.
Single to end the over. Babar Azam taps this away behind point and keeps strike. An excellent first over from Blessing comes to an end.
Works it away with the wrists on the leg side for nothing.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, Azam hangs his bat inside the line and gets beaten.
Fullish in length on off stump, blocked with a straight bat in defense.
Almost! Could have been another edge behind. Short of a length outside off, Babar half-heartedly slashes at this. It goes past the edge and behind to the keeper.
Wide! Fires it well outside off, it's too far out and across the tramline, so the umpire signals a wide.
Babar Azam walks in next to bat.

OUT! Gone first ball! Won't really count for much, probably, but something to excite the Zimbabwean fans! Blessing Muzarabani is right on the money with this. Sharp bumper going across on off, Imam-ul-Haq is completely taken by surprise as he can't do anything about it. Hangs his bat up, gets an edge and it's taken by the keeper behind. Superb start from the tall pacer.
The players are back. 68 needed to win. Just 300 balls in hand. Fakhar Zaman and Imam-ul-Haq walk out as the opening pair. Blessing Muzarabani will bowl first up to Imam. Here we go...
